items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: The one who probably can answer it, of course, is Pee Wee. And Pee Wee probably could give you a very clear-cut answer on that.

ctx.x: That influence kept bobbing up, even into the 30s, and thinned out soon after when it became more respectable for pure tone. But I've wondered whether Tesh, finding the raspy and the hard tone so full of emotion, might have related to Bechet or to Dodds, who were so capable in using the expressive distortion of tone. And to say that it probably was a sequence isn't quite as accurate as knowing that it was. And so this question will continue to bob up.
The one who probably can answer it, of course, is Pee Wee. And Pee Wee probably could give you a very clear-cut answer on that.
Did Bud Freeman relate at all to the colored influences?
